result.title: Generalizing Metropolis-Hastings for DAG Sampling
result.summary: A fundamental challenge in Bayesian network structure learning lies in efficiently approximating the posterior distribution of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). For large, high-dimensional datasets, the task remains beyond the capabilities of current methods. This work advances Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms by introducing novel moves that simultaneously resample the parents for multiple nodes of the DAG. At the core of these moves is duet sampling, a new generalization of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm that selects two proposal distributions from a pool at each iteration. One is used for generating a candidate state of the Markov chain and another for evaluating the return to the current state; both are ingredients of an appropriately crafted acceptance criterion. Pairing different proposal distributions provides additional freedom and enables constructing Markov chains that mix more efficiently than their basic Metropolis-Hastings counterparts, at no additional computational cost. Experiments show that our new moves, both individually and in combination, outperform the previous state of the art, which relies on a more restrictive pool of moves. This advantage persists even when letting the previous methods leverage duet sampling to enhance their performance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 duet sampling：在每次迭代中从提议池选两个分布，一个用于生成候选 DAG 状态，另一个用于评估返回当前状态，并据此设计可同时重采样多个节点父节点的 MCMC moves，以更高效地逼近 DAG 后验。
AI.relevance_reason: 把候选状态生成与返回评估分成两个提议分布的做法，可能为 latent 推理中候选推理状态的生成／验证分工、以及状态空间搜索与停止准则提供类比线索，但与本主线距离较远，需核查其可迁移性。
